classification.difficultyReason: Select the matching central and circumference angles, including marked reflex angles; the hardest parts require recognising a diameter, inferring a right angle and using the triangle angle sum.

content.prompt: Find the value of $x$ in these circles.

spec.description: Two radii and two chords subtending the same arc; centre marked.
spec.mathematics: The central angle is 100 degrees; the corresponding circumference angle is x.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the given 100 degrees and unknown x are visible.

answer.worked:
The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference standing on the same arc.
$$\begin{align*}x&=100^\circ\div2\\x&=50^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Radii to top and upper-right points; chords meet at a bottom-left point. A leader identifies the narrow circumference angle.
spec.mathematics: The circumference angle is 20 degrees; its corresponding central angle is x.
spec.answerVisibility: Only 20 degrees and x are visible.

answer.worked:
The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference standing on the same arc.
$$\begin{align*}x&=2\times20^\circ\\x&=40^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Radii to left and bottom points, with chords meeting at a lower-right point.
spec.mathematics: The circumference angle is 40 degrees; the central angle on the same arc is x.
spec.answerVisibility: Only 40 degrees and x are visible.

answer.worked:
The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference standing on the same arc.
$$\begin{align*}x&=2\times40^\circ\\x&=80^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Two radii subtend the upper arc; chords meet at a lower-right circumference point. The displaced 120-degree label has a leader to the central sector.
spec.mathematics: The central angle is 120 degrees and the corresponding circumference angle is x.
spec.answerVisibility: Only 120 degrees and x are visible.

answer.worked:
The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference standing on the same arc.
$$\begin{align*}x&=120^\circ\div2\\x&=60^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: The circumference vertex lies on the minor arc. The unknown central angle is explicitly marked as reflex around the left and bottom of the centre.
spec.mathematics: The 125-degree circumference angle stands on the major arc; x is the corresponding reflex central angle.
spec.answerVisibility: Only 125 degrees and reflex x are visible.

answer.worked:
The reflex angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference standing on the same major arc.
$$\begin{align*}x&=2\times125^\circ\\x&=250^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Radii meet lower-left and lower-right endpoints; chords meet at a bottom point on the minor arc. A reflex central arc passes above the centre.
spec.mathematics: The reflex central angle is 225 degrees; x is the circumference angle on the same major arc.
spec.answerVisibility: Only 225 degrees and x are visible.

answer.worked:
The angle at the circumference is half the reflex angle at the centre standing on the same major arc.
$$\begin{align*}x&=225^\circ\div2\\x&=112.5^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Downward radii and chords from an upper-left vertex. A curved leader connects 76 degrees to the central sector, clear of the chord crossing.
spec.mathematics: The central angle is 76 degrees; the corresponding circumference angle is x.
spec.answerVisibility: Only 76 degrees and x are visible.

answer.worked:
The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference standing on the same arc.
$$\begin{align*}x&=76^\circ\div2\\x&=38^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Upper radii and chords meeting at a top vertex on the minor arc; the central marker explicitly follows the reflex sector below the centre.
spec.mathematics: The reflex central angle is 240 degrees; x stands on the same major arc.
spec.answerVisibility: Only 240 degrees and x are visible.

answer.worked:
The angle at the circumference is half the reflex angle at the centre standing on the same major arc.
$$\begin{align*}x&=240^\circ\div2\\x&=120^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Two narrow angles with separate leaders. The long chord is offset from the centre and is not a diameter.
spec.mathematics: The central angle is 36 degrees; the corresponding top circumference angle is x.
spec.answerVisibility: Only 36 degrees and x are visible.

answer.worked:
The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference standing on the same arc.
$$\begin{align*}x&=36^\circ\div2\\x&=18^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Inscribed triangle whose left-lower to upper-right side is a diameter through the marked centre. No supplied right-angle square.
spec.mathematics: The upper-right angle is 20 degrees and the left-lower angle is x; the third angle is in a semicircle.
spec.answerVisibility: Only 20 degrees and x are visible; the inferred right angle is not drawn.

answer.worked:
The angle opposite the diameter is $90^\circ$ (angle in a semicircle). Using the angle sum of a triangle:
$$\begin{align*}x&=180^\circ-90^\circ-20^\circ\\x&=70^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Inscribed triangle with upper-left to lower-right diameter through the marked centre. No supplied right-angle square.
spec.mathematics: The upper-left angle is 65 degrees, the lower-right angle is x, and the top angle stands on the diameter.
spec.answerVisibility: Only 65 degrees and x are visible; the inferred right angle is not drawn.

answer.worked:
The angle opposite the diameter is $90^\circ$ (angle in a semicircle). Using the angle sum of a triangle:
$$\begin{align*}x&=180^\circ-90^\circ-65^\circ\\x&=25^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Inscribed triangle with a top-to-bottom diameter through the marked centre, a short top chord, and a leader to the narrow bottom angle. No supplied right-angle square.
spec.mathematics: The top angle is 80 degrees and the bottom angle is x; the upper-right angle stands on the diameter.
spec.answerVisibility: Only 80 degrees and x are visible; the inferred right angle is not drawn.

answer.worked:
The angle opposite the diameter is $90^\circ$ (angle in a semicircle). Using the angle sum of a triangle:
$$\begin{align*}x&=180^\circ-90^\circ-80^\circ\\x&=10^\circ\end{align*}$$
